subject: Post-call: HorizonAI token profile & concurrency plan
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap - token volumes, concurrency, next steps

Claire — thanks for the 30-min call earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can size options and pricing for the POC.

Key takeaways (from our notes):
- Monthly volume (target range): you mentioned roughly 120M - 250M input+output tokens/month.
- Typical request envelope: ~300-600 tokens per call (prompt + completion), with some outliers up to ~2k tokens for longer synth tasks.
- Traffic pattern: steady baseline (20-40 rps across regional endpoints) with two daily peak windows (~2x baseline) and occasional spikes for batch exports.
- Concurrency: average concurrent in-flight requests ~30, peak concurrent observed ~120.
- Latency SLO target: 95th <= 250ms for short-turn queries, best-effort for long generative jobs.

Open asks / info we need from your side:
1) Can you share a 7-day sample traffic profile (timestamped requests with request token counts) — CSV is fine. This lets us estimate continuous-batching benefits and KV cache hit rates.
2) Confirm budget target as a rough $/1M tokens target range (you mentioned a ballpark on the call) so we can show Hosted vs Dedicated cost bands.
3) Any restrictions on model variants (must be open-weights, or can we use quantized variants)?

What we will provide next:
- A conservative costing example for Hosted and Dedicated covering high/medium/low consumption and concurrency buckets.
- A proposal for a 7-day technical trial (metered, with traffic routing instructions) and minimal legal/POC doc.
- Suggested batching & cache config to hit your latency + cost targets (initial recommendation included in attached MAP draft).

Attachments: MAP_horizon-draft.xlsx (workback plan + milestones)

Proposed next step: please send the 7-day traffic sample (CSV) and confirm if legal wants a draft SOW/POC first. If convenient, I can book a 30-min follow-up Tuesday to review sizing with your infra team.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

— Markus

Markus — thanks for the summary and the MAP. I'm attaching a trimmed sample of our traffic as requested (Horizon_Traffic_Profile_Mar.csv). A few clarifications on our end: 

- Monthly tokens: the 120M - 250M is accurate; Q2 PTO projection is toward the upper bound if our new feature launches.
- Request sizes: 75% of requests are in the 300-450 token range, ~20% between 450-900, and the remainder are longer batch jobs.
- Concurrency: baseline ~30, typical peaks to ~120 for interactive inference; batch export jobs are handled separately and can be scheduled.
- Budget: our procurement target is in the neighborhood of $1,200 per 1M tokens (covers model + inference) but we have flexibility +/-15% depending on SLA and unit economics on long runs.
- Model constraints: open-weight quantized models are fine; we prefer not to use proprietary closed-hosted-only models.

Legal/procurement note: Please include a short POC SOW and estimated cost delta for a Dedicated reserved pool vs Hosted metered. Procurement wants to see a not-to-exceed cap for the trial. I'll loop in LegalOps once we have a short POC doc.

Attached: Horizon_Traffic_Profile_Mar.csv

Happy to do the Tue slot — let's tentatively take 10:30 AM PT.

— Claire

Subject: Re: Post-call recap - token volumes, concurrency, next steps

Claire — thanks for the CSV and the clear budget guidance. A couple of technical notes and a concrete cost example so procurement has numbers to review.

Technical assumptions (how Redwood would approach this workload):
- Continuous batching: because ~75% of your traffic sits in a narrow token window, we expect continuous prefix pooling and batching to yield a 25%-45% token-cost reduction compared to naively metered short-running calls. This assumes steady arrival rates and ~60-80% prefix reuse in the model paths.
- KV cache: for multi-turn sessions and reranking, KV cache improves tail latency on repeated contexts and reduces token compute on the model side (helpful for higher per-request token ranges).
- Concurrency handling: for peaks to 120 concurrent requests we recommend Dedicated with configured autoscale headroom (burst to Hosted) to maintain 95th-latency SLAs. Hosted can handle the lower ranges but will show higher cost per 1M at sustained peak.

Sample unit economics (illustrative — final numbers in official quote):
- Hosted (metered): conservative estimate $1,150 - $1,450 / 1M tokens at your workload profile (no reserved discount; includes streaming and model weights).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): with a 12-month commit and quantized model profile we can be in the $820 - $1,050 / 1M tokens band depending on effective batch factor and KV hit rate.
- POC (7-day trial): we can cap the trial at a not-to-exceed of $5k and run your live traffic through a mirrored routing for comparison. We'll provide a short telemetry export showing per-token cost and latency percentiles.

Next steps (proposed):
1) We'll send a short POC SOW and a 7-day trial quote (attached). Please confirm LegalOps contact and the acceptable cap for the POC.
2) Laura from Solutions will join Tuesday's sizing call (10:30 AM PT) to walk the infra team through expected batching behavior and test harness.
3) If you approve the cap, we'll spin the trial environment and provide an ingestion guide for mirrored traffic.

Attachment: 7day-trial-quote.pdf

TL;DR: With continuous batching and quantization we should be able to materially improve unit economics versus pure Hosted; Dedicated gives the best long-run $/1M at scale. We'll surface concrete quote bands once legal/procurement confirms the desired commitment level.

— Markus
